arms.label: Ember
evidence: Preserves the Pi 5, Active Cooler, NVMe-under-Pi stack and complete native interface inventory while explicitly retaining the actual display, NVMe board, SSD, and peripherals as unknowns.
Verified facts, reasonable design assumptions, provisional dimensions, and unresolved measurements are consistently separated.
The filtered front intake splits across the display/CPU plenum and NVMe channel, reunites before the rear exhaust, and includes sealing against recirculation.
Both fans have stated direction and separate control ownership, with tach monitoring, noise testing, dirty-filter obstruction testing, and an exhaust-failure response.
Daily USB/Ethernet, rear power/video, microSD, internal unused interfaces, strain relief, bend envelopes, and whole-stack versus Pi-only rotation are coherently addressed.
Filter, rear fan, NVMe, display, cables, and the slide-out carrier have distinct service paths; the Active Cooler remains installed during recovery and reassembly.
The 24-degree screen, five controls, rear/right cable exits, acoustic checks, broad support polygon, and touch/controller testing support repeated musical use.
The response clearly distinguishes the generated concept from measured hardware, CAD fit, thermal capacity, acoustic performance, electrical integrity, and production proof.
Fit, thermal, airflow, acoustic, power, cable, fault, and interaction tests are specific, but there is no explicit post-service untouched-state/reassembly verification.

The image strongly agrees with the design: five keys, front grille, correct side and rear connector groups, rear fan, and a cutaway showing both airflow branches and the NVMe stack form one coherent product.
arms.most_consequential_strength: The most complete text-to-image package: its cutaway makes the claimed component stack and front-to-rear split airflow directly legible.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: Despite excellent image agreement, verification does not explicitly confirm that repeated servicing and reassembly preserve configuration, cables, and prior working state.

arms.label: Harbor
evidence: Correctly inventories the Pi 5 and Active Cooler, preserves the unidentified hardware as unknown, and labels the RC070N, NVMe Base, and rear fan as packaging assumptions.
Verified repository and Pi facts, landscape inference, explicit assumptions, provisional targets, and unresolved items remain distinct.
Upper display/CPU and lower NVMe paths receive filtered intake, merge at a sealed rear exhaust, and include measures against connector-pocket bypass and recirculation.
The Active Cooler retains native ownership while the exhaust has independent PWM/tach control, fail-full-speed behavior, rearward direction, obstruction tests, and acoustic evaluation.
Daily side ports, rear power/video/display connections, service-only interfaces, cable clamps, plug envelopes, and complete-assembly rotation consequences are detailed.
Separate access exists for the filter, fan and cables, bottom Pi/NVMe sled, microSD, and screen cassette while preserving the fitted Active Cooler.
Viewing angle, eight tactile controls, protected cable gutter, recording-load acoustics, touch loading, cable pulls, and tip resistance work together credibly.
It explicitly calls the image an appearance reference rather than CAD and keeps nominal measurements, thermal targets, acoustics, electrical integration, and manufacturability unproven.
The test plan is specific across fit, thermal, fan faults, airflow, acoustics, power, cables, RF, and safety, but lacks a defined repeated-service/untouched-state check.

The render presents a coherent wedge, intake, eight keys, power control, side ports, rear fan, and rear Pi port group, but it does not visibly provide the separately powered display USB-C connection required by the prose.
arms.most_consequential_strength: A particularly strong treatment of the ambiguous display connectors, separate power requirements, and two-fan control and failure behavior.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: Image/design agreement is incomplete: the rear rendering shows one USB-C and two HDMI-class sockets, while the selected display strategy requires an additional accessible display-power USB-C connection.

arms.label: Quartz
evidence: The Pi, cooler, and NVMe details are mostly correct, but the package resolves the reported two USB-C connectors as mistaken micro-HDMI and substitutes a GPIO HyperPixel plus custom hub, instead of preserving that physical-display uncertainty.
It uses clear verified, inferred, assumed, and unresolved sections, but the unsupported resolution of the reported USB-C hardware blurs an open constraint into a fact.
The two intake bands coherently serve the display/cooler and Pi/NVMe channels, with a splitter, rear exhaust, sealed connector hood, and recirculation control.
Direction, independent fan ownership, fail-full-speed control, tach monitoring, obstruction/failure tests, vibration treatment, and microphone-oriented noise checks are all covered.
Direct and hub-derived daily ports, service and unused connectors, strain envelopes, dust shutters, and whole-stack versus independent rotation are comprehensively addressed.
The removable filter and fan hatch, bottom electronics cassette, display cassette, NVMe access, cable routing, and retained Active Cooler provide nondestructive recovery.

Cable paths, five keys, stability targets, touch and keyboard recovery, and acoustic testing are good, but the dense 40×13 musician interface on a four-inch screen weakens sustained viewing and reach.
All physical dimensions are provisional, the render is not treated as proof, and CAD, fit, thermal, acoustic, electrical, and manufacturing evidence remain explicitly outstanding.
The risk table supplies precise fit, thermal, airflow-fault, acoustic, electrical, cable, interface, dust, stability, and ten-cycle service checks.

The image closely matches the chosen compact product—five-key rail, intake bands, right patch bay, rear exhaust, USB-C/two-HDMI hood, and heel—although that coherence faithfully depicts the questionable substituted hardware baseline.
arms.most_consequential_strength: The verification package is unusually concrete, including ten service cycles, microphone-noise measurement, loaded-filter testing, and full interface recovery checks.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The visually coherent image reinforces the central fidelity problem: a newly assumed four-inch GPIO display replaces rather than preserves the unresolved display and its reported USB-C connectors.

arms.label: Willow
evidence: Preserves the Pi 5, Active Cooler, NVMe stack and full native connector inventory while keeping the actual display, its two reported USB-C functions, SSD, and existing fan explicitly unknown.
Verified facts, reasonable inferences, explicit assumptions, provisional geometry, and unresolved implementation items are cleanly separated.
Filtered front flow divides between the display/Active-Cooler plenum and NVMe bypass, rejoins at the rear fan, and uses sealed seams to prevent exhaust recirculation.
The cooler retains firmware control while the exhaust has separate fused PWM/tach ownership; outward direction, stalls, blockage, noise, and control behavior are tested.
Daily right-side ports, rear power/service video, internal unused interfaces, strain-managed raceways, and complete-stack rotation alternatives are coherently resolved.
The sliding filter, fan access, bottom Pi/NVMe cassette, separate display carrier, cable service loops, and retained Active Cooler support state-preserving maintenance.
The 28-degree display, tactile controller row, side/rear cable routes, recording-position acoustics, ballasted stance, and repeated mechanical tests support musician use.
The proposal expressly withholds claims of fit, temperature, noise, strength, EMC, and manufacturability while separating surrogate measurements and validation targets.
Specific hardware audit, electrical, display, thermal, fan-fault, smoke-flow, acoustic, cable, repeated-service, mechanical, and wireless checks cover the full verification scope.

The exterior, side ports, rear fan and service bay read as one product, but the image shows nine equally spaced controls rather than eight plus a visually separated power key, and its visible front openings do not clearly match the specified five louvers.
arms.most_consequential_strength: The written package combines strong unknown-hardware discipline with complete service and validation treatment, including repeated-service testing.
arms.most_consequential_weakness: The principal weakness is image/design disagreement: the promised separated power control and five-louver front are not faithfully represented in the otherwise polished render.

comparative_result: Ember and Willow tie at 39/40. Ember has the strongest visual explanation and image agreement; Willow has the stronger explicit repeated-service verification. Harbor follows at 38 because its rear render omits a connection required by its selected display strategy. Quartz scores 36: it is highly coherent and testable, but its substituted four-inch GPIO display weakens hardware fidelity and musician usability.
disagreements: The closest judgment is between Ember and Willow: Ember is visually more faithful, while Willow more explicitly verifies service recovery. Harbor's missing rendered display-power connection and Quartz's treatment of the reported USB-C connectors are substantive package-level discrepancies rather than cosmetic preferences.
